reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it promotes a creator-run giveaway offering two selected participants $50 Nike gift cards under stated drawing dates and prize terms. Participation involves subscribing, commenting, and liking videos, with no stated investment, payment, credential request, or other financial transaction. The records do not establish whether the drawing occurred or whether the gift cards were delivered.

citations.quote: with the hundred dollars giveaway just like last time it'll be two winners to $50 Gift cards to Nike so you guys can use them at the outlet all you have to do to be in the contest is be a subscriber and comment your name and you have to like all of the american tv videos
There will be 2 winners chosen from his raffle December 8th at 3 pm! The winners will receive 1 ($50 Nike Gift Card) each!
make sure you guys sign up for the $100 raffle to Nike

opening.argument: Judge, the prize is presented as the reason to perform a set of channel-building actions. The speaker offers two $50 Nike gift cards, then makes entry depend on subscribing, commenting a name, and liking the channel's videos. That is a low-barrier reward tied directly to viewer action. Calling the actions free does not remove the solicitation: viewers are asked to deliver engagement before any winner is chosen.

citations.quote: with the hundred dollars giveaway just like last time it'll be two winners to $50 Gift cards to Nike so you guys can use them at the outlet
all you have to do to be in the contest is be a subscriber and comment your name and you have to like all of the american tv videos

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense accurately identifies the prize and drawing date, but those details do not answer what the prize is used to obtain. The speaker calls subscribing, liking every video, and commenting a name the conditions for entry. No payment request is needed for the reward to function as an inducement to act, and the stated drawing date does not establish that a prize was awarded.

citations.quote: You have to be a subscriber, you have to like all of the Marron TV videos, and comment your name below on this video or on my Instagram, Facebook, Twitter.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The link between a prize and entry actions is real, but it is also how an ordinary giveaway works. The speaker states the number and value of the prizes and describes a drawing; the cited conditions are subscribing, liking, and commenting, not paying or surrendering credentials. The opening supplies no evidence that the promised cards are fictitious or that entrants face a hidden demand.

citations.quote: There will be 2 winners chosen from his raffle December 8th at 3 pm! The winners will receive 1 ($50 Nike Gift Card) each!
i'll do a drawing

opening.argument: Consider the signals together: a headline advertising a free $100 value, gift cards for two winners, and a specific time when winners will supposedly be announced. The speaker also invokes a past giveaway, but this record does not verify that earlier award or show delivery of these cards. The date gives viewers a reason to enter promptly while the reward remains a promise. That combination warrants treating the offer as a potentially deceptive prize solicitation, even without an upfront charge.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense relies on the stated prize terms, but a stated plan to draw winners is not evidence that the gift cards exist or will be delivered. Nor does the absence of a payment request settle whether a free-prize pitch is misleading. The earlier giveaway is asserted by the speaker, not corroborated by the cited material.

citations.quote: I've done a giveaway in the past and I want to do one for you guys.
i'll announce the winners on my instagram just like last time i'll do a drawing

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The opening identifies uncertainty, not deception. A free prize, a scheduled drawing, and a speaker's account of a prior giveaway are compatible with an ordinary promotion. This record cannot confirm delivery, but it also supplies no failed claim, payment demand, or other evidence that the drawing is a pretext. The stated offer remains two $50 gift cards awarded to selected entrants.

citations.quote: There will be 2 winners chosen from his raffle December 8th at 3 pm! The winners will receive 1 ($50 Nike Gift Card) each!
That's the only stipulation. You have to be a subscriber, you have to like all of the Marron TV videos, and comment your name below on this video or on my Instagram, Facebook, Twitter.

opening.argument: The speaker frames the video as a 20-video anniversary and thanks supporters, but the operative message steers viewers toward channel and social-media participation. He says he hopes to reach 300 subscribers, asks entrants to like every video, and accepts names through the video or his social accounts. The Nike-card offer gives those requests an incentive. Judge the video by that solicitation, not just by its celebratory tone: it uses a promised reward to recruit repeated engagement across the creator's channels.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls this a creator-run giveaway, but that description does not account for the speaker's stated subscriber goal or the requirement to like all his videos. The prize is doing promotional work for the channel. A date and prize amount describe the proposed reward; they do not establish that the resulting engagement is incidental or that the cards were delivered.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The video plainly promotes the creator's channel, but promotion is not itself evidence of a scam. The speaker makes the engagement conditions explicit and says he will select winners in a drawing. The opening shows an incentive to gain subscribers and likes, not a concealed transaction or evidence that the promised prizes are false.
